title: Ambiguity orientation
description: Whether an explicitly bounded numeric probability interval is treated as sufficient to act or as a reason to seek one precise probability, distinct from payoff sensitivity, ordinary risk preference, and epistemic uncertainty about missing evidence.

contrast_conditions.label: Proceed with a bounded interval
contrast_conditions.definition: The decision maker treats an explicitly bounded numeric probability interval as usable information and proceeds without first obtaining one precise probability.

contrast_conditions.label: Seek one precise probability
contrast_conditions.definition: The decision maker treats the same explicitly bounded numeric probability interval as a reason to obtain one precise probability before committing.

probe_prompt_template:
Read the following short decision scenario. Track how the decision maker handles a bounded numeric probability interval separately from the attractiveness and size of the possible outcomes.

Scenario:
{scenario}

Continue processing the scenario.

independent_behavior_task.prompt_template: Consider a separate allocation decision between one lottery with a stated probability and one lottery with an explicitly stated bounded numeric probability interval, such as 30–50%. Allocate exactly 100 points between the two options without requesting any additional information. Return exactly two integers on separate lines: first the allocation to the known-probability option and second the allocation to the interval-probability option; the two integers must sum to 100. Use new domains, stakes, and item identifiers, and do not ask the model to label its decision style.
independence_requirements: Use new domains, actors, stakes, and lottery identifiers not present in probe prompts.
Cross the stated-probability option's quality, the bounded-interval option's quality, payoff scale, and numeric interval width independently.
Do not ask the model to classify ambiguity tolerance, ambiguity aversion, epistemic uncertainty, or any construct condition.

expected_by_lottery_quality.quality_matched: proceed-with-interval and seek-precision conditions are compared within each crossed option-quality, payoff-scale, and interval-width cell
expected_by_lottery_quality.quality_crossed: estimate the orientation contrast after accounting for independently crossed option quality, payoff scale, and numeric interval width

behavior.warning: This construct concerns willingness to act under underspecified probabilities, not generic risk seeking, payoff preference, or numerical uncertainty competence.

metadata.primary_question: Is an orientation toward acting under unresolved probabilities decodable, and does it transfer to an independent known-versus-underspecified lottery allocation?
